title: Installing Linux — Starting from Linux (dd)
why: If your current machine already runs Linux, the dd command is the most straightforward way to create a bootable USB drive. It copies the ISO image byte-by-byte to the device, producing a perfect bootable copy. No additional software is needed — dd is included in every Linux distribution.

instructions.text: Download the Ubuntu Server ISO from the official website (https://ubuntu.com/download/server). Choose the latest LTS version for stability.
Insert a USB drive (at least 4 GB) into your Linux machine. WARNING: All data on this USB drive will be erased.
Identify your USB device. List all block devices and find your USB drive — it is typically /dev/sdb or /dev/sdc. Do NOT select your system disk.
instructions.note: Look for the device that matches the size of your USB drive. Never use /dev/sda if that is your system disk.

instructions.text: Unmount the USB drive if it was auto-mounted.
instructions.note: Replace /dev/sdX with your actual USB device (e.g. /dev/sdb).

instructions.text: Write the ISO image to the USB drive using dd.
instructions.command: sudo dd if=ubuntu-24.04-live-server-amd64.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress conv=fsync
instructions.note: Replace /dev/sdX with your actual USB device. The conv=fsync ensures all data is flushed to the drive. This will take a few minutes.

instructions.text: Verify the write completed successfully. The dd command will output the number of bytes written.
Insert the USB drive into your home server and boot from it. You may need to change the boot order in your BIOS/UEFI settings (usually accessed by pressing F2, F12, DEL, or ESC during boot).
Follow the Ubuntu Server installer. Choose your language, keyboard layout, and network configuration. For the disk setup, using the entire disk with LVM is recommended for flexibility.
Create your user account and set a strong password. Enable OpenSSH server when prompted — we will configure it further later.
After installation completes, remove the USB drive and reboot. Log in with the credentials you created.
Update the system to ensure all packages are current.
instructions.command: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

questions.text: Why is Linux preferred over Windows for a home server?
options: Linux is free, open-source, stable, and has excellent networking and server support
Linux comes pre-installed on most hardware
Linux does not require any updates

questions.text: What does the 'dd' command do when creating a bootable USB?
options: It downloads the ISO file from the internet
It formats the USB drive to NTFS
It copies the ISO image byte-by-byte to the USB device
It installs Linux directly onto the server

questions.text: Why is it critical to identify the correct device before running dd?
options: dd will not work on the wrong device
dd overwrites the target device completely — selecting the wrong one could destroy your system
The wrong device will be too slow
dd requires a specific device name format
